concepts: locating physical features on outline map of India
NE monsoon wind direction and Mumbai High location
questions.question: On the outline map of India provided mark and name the following: (i) Vindhya Mountains (ii) River Yamuna (iii) Kolkata (iv) Kanchenjunga (v) Lake Chilika (vi) Konkan coastal plain (vii) Thar Desert (viii) Gulf of Khambhat (ix) Mark with arrows the direction of North East Monsoon Winds (x) Mumbai High
questions.solution: Outline map of India, mark and name (model answer for locations; the board paper prints a marked map, not text): (i) Vindhya Mountains: east-west range in central India, north of the Narmada, across Madhya Pradesh. (ii) River Yamuna: from Yamunotri (Uttarakhand) past Delhi and Agra, joining the Ganga at Prayagraj (Uttar Pradesh). (iii) Kolkata: on the Hooghly river, West Bengal, about 22.6 deg N, 88.4 deg E. (iv) Kanchenjunga: Sikkim-Nepal border, about 27.7 deg N, 88.1 deg E. (v) Lake Chilika: Odisha coast, Bay of Bengal, south of the Mahanadi delta. (vi) Konkan coastal plain: west coast strip from Daman to Goa. (vii) Thar Desert: western Rajasthan, west of the Aravallis. (viii) Gulf of Khambhat: inlet of the Arabian Sea on the Gujarat coast, east of the Saurashtra peninsula. (ix) North-East Monsoon winds: arrows from the north-east over the Bay of Bengal towards the Tamil Nadu coast. (x) Mumbai High: offshore oil field in the Arabian Sea, about 160 km north-west of Mumbai.

marking_points.point: Correctly marked and named: Vindhya Mountains
Correctly marked and named: River Yamuna
Correctly marked and named: Kolkata
Correctly marked and named: Kanchenjunga
Correctly marked and named: Lake Chilika
Correctly marked and named: Konkan coastal plain
Correctly marked and named: Thar Desert
Correctly marked and named: Gulf of Khambhat
Correctly marked and named: Arrows showing direction of North East Monsoon Winds
Correctly marked and named: Mumbai High

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Give any one use of Copper.
questions.solution: As a good conductor of heat and electricity, copper is mostly used in electrical equipment as wiring and in motors.

marking_points.point: Any one correct use of copper (e.g. wiring/motors as good conductor of heat and electricity)

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
concepts: distribution of iron ore in India
questions.question: Name two Indian states in which iron ore is found in abundance.
questions.solution: Any two: Jharkhand, Odisha (Orissa), Chhattisgarh, Goa, Maharashtra, Karnataka.

marking_points.point: Any two correct states (Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Maharashtra, Karnataka)

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: With reference to Hirakud project: On which river is it based?
questions.solution: River Mahanadi.

marking_points.point: River Mahanadi

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: With reference to Hirakud project: Name an Indian state benefitted by Hirakud project.
questions.solution: Odisha.

marking_points.point: Odisha

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Give three disadvantages of using coal.
questions.solution: (a) Non-renewable resource; excess use can lead to exhaustion in the near future. (b) Use of coal results in air pollution. (c) Calorific value of coal is low, so it is not a very efficient fuel.

marking_points.point: Non-renewable; may be exhausted in near future
Causes air pollution
Low calorific value, not an efficient fuel

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Mention two advantages of nuclear power.
questions.solution: (i) A large amount of energy can be generated from a small amount of nuclear fuel such as uranium and plutonium. (ii) It emits the least amount of carbon and so causes less air pollution.

marking_points.point: Large energy from small amount of fuel (uranium, plutonium)
Emits least carbon / less air pollution

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: What is the advantage of using solar energy in place of the conventional sources of energy?
questions.solution: It is clean and pollution free; it is renewable; it reduces dependency on conventional sources such as coal and petroleum. (Any one.)

marking_points.point: Any one valid advantage: clean/pollution free, renewable, or reduces dependency on coal and petroleum

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Mention two problems faced by the agriculture sector of India.
questions.solution: (1) Low yield, 30%-50% lower than developed nations; excessive fertilizer use decreases soil fertility. (2) Average farm size is less than 1 hectare, so farms lack new technologies and best farming methods. (3) Ineffective irrigation, unavailability of credit and lack of nutrients in the soil. (Any two.)

marking_points.point: First valid problem (e.g. low yield / soil fertility loss)
Second valid problem (e.g. small farm size, poor irrigation, lack of credit)

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Mention any one climatic condition found suitable for growing cotton.
questions.solution: Warm climate: summer temperature 21-27 deg C, abundant sunshine and 210 frost-free days; or moderate to light rainfall of 50-80 cm. (Any one.)

marking_points.point: Any one correct climatic condition (warm 21-27 deg C with sunshine and 210 frost-free days, or 50-80 cm rainfall)

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Name the state that is the leading producer of cotton in India.
questions.solution: Gujarat and Maharashtra are the leading producers of cotton in India (accept either).

marking_points.point: Gujarat (or Maharashtra)

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: With reference to Rice cultivation: Name the soil found suitable for its growth.
questions.solution: Silt clay loam, silt clay and clay.

marking_points.point: Silt clay loam / silt clay / clay

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: With reference to Rice cultivation: Name the state that is the largest producer of this crop in India.
questions.solution: West Bengal.

marking_points.point: West Bengal

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: With reference to Rice cultivation: In which cropping season is it generally grown in India?
questions.solution: Kharif season; sown in June or July and harvested in November and December.

marking_points.point: Kharif

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Name the state that is the largest producer of sugarcane in India.
questions.solution: Uttar Pradesh.

marking_points.point: Uttar Pradesh

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Why more than two ratoon crops are not advisable for sugarcane farmers?
questions.solution: It yields thinner sugarcane with low sugar content and increases the risk of pests and diseases.

marking_points.point: Thinner cane with low sugar content / increased risk of pests and diseases

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: What is Zayad cropping season?
questions.solution: A short duration cropping season that usually occurs between the Rabi and Kharif seasons, ranging from March to June.

marking_points.point: Short-duration season between Rabi and Kharif (March to June)

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Differentiate between mineral based and agro-based industry giving suitable example for each from India.
questions.solution: Mineral based industries use mineral ores as raw material and are usually capital intensive; example Tata Steel Limited (iron ore). Agro-based industries use plant and animal products as raw material and do not require huge capital; example Dalmia Bharat Sugar & Industries Ltd (sugarcane).

marking_points.point: Mineral based industry uses mineral ores and is capital intensive, with an Indian example (e.g. Tata Steel)
Agro-based industry uses plant/animal products and needs less capital, with an Indian example (e.g. sugar industry)

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Give two ways in which petrochemical industry is important for India.
questions.solution: (1) It meets the large energy demand of the agricultural and industrial sectors, aiding their growth. (2) It provides synthetic fibres and polymers used as raw material for furniture, automobile, clothing, construction, housing, packaging, medical appliances and other industries.

marking_points.point: Fulfils energy demand of agriculture and industry
Provides synthetic fibres/polymers as raw material for other industries

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: With reference to Tata Steel plant: Where is it located?
questions.solution: Jamshedpur district of Jharkhand.

marking_points.point: Jamshedpur, Jharkhand

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: With reference to Tata Steel plant: From where does it get its coal requirements?
questions.solution: Jharia and Bokaro coalfields of Jharkhand.

marking_points.point: Jharia and Bokaro coalfields

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
concepts: iron ore source for Tata Steel
questions.question: With reference to Tata Steel plant: From where does it get its iron ore requirements?
questions.solution: Gorumahisani mines in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, and Noamundi mines in Singhbhum district, Jharkhand.

marking_points.point: Gorumahisani (Mayurbhanj, Odisha) / Noamundi (Singhbhum, Jharkhand)

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Name any two by products of the sugar industry.
questions.solution: Any two: molasses, bagasse, press mud.

marking_points.point: First by-product (molasses/bagasse/press mud)
Second by-product

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
concepts: location factors of cotton textile industry
questions.question: Why are the cotton textile industries mostly located in the coastal areas?
questions.solution: The humid climate of coastal regions is suitable for spinning, and moisture in the air increases the strength of the cotton thread.

marking_points.point: Humid climate suits spinning; moisture in air increases strength of cotton

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Mention two advantages of using roadways.
questions.solution: Any two: door-to-door service; lesser risk of damage in transit; services even to rural areas; flexibility; suitable for shorter distances; cheaper; feeder for other means of transport.

marking_points.point: First valid advantage
Second valid advantage

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: What is the purpose of developing the Golden Quadrilateral in India?
questions.solution: It connects major cities and ports by a faster transport network; provides better access to markets from smaller towns; reduces agricultural spoilage in transport.

marking_points.point: Connects major cities and ports by faster network
Better market access from smaller towns / reduces agricultural spoilage

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Mention three disadvantages of waterways.
questions.solution: Slowest means of transport; navigation is difficult during monsoon; fear of sinking; not suitable for small businesses. (Any three.)

marking_points.point: First valid disadvantage
Second valid disadvantage
Third valid disadvantage

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Give a reason: Railways are not well developed in the North Eastern States of India.
questions.solution: The region has highly undulating terrain, big rivers and dense forests that make laying track difficult; it is also prone to natural calamities, making construction harder.

marking_points.point: Undulating terrain, big rivers, dense forests make track laying difficult / prone to natural calamities

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Give a reason: Air transport has gained popularity in recent times in India.
questions.solution: It is the fastest means of transport, the most comfortable way of transit, and caters to emergency services. (Any one.)

marking_points.point: Fastest/most comfortable/caters to emergency services

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Give a reason: NSEW is helpful for India.
questions.solution: The North-South East-West corridor is a key project of the Indian highway network because it connects important manufacturing units, commercial hubs and cultural centres of India.

marking_points.point: Connects manufacturing units, commercial hubs and cultural centres

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Why is there a need for waste management in large metropolitan cities?
questions.solution: Metropolitan cities generate enormous quantities of solid waste every day, and open dumping breeds flies, mosquitoes and disease and pollutes land, water and air; landfill dumping also releases methane, adding to air pollution and the greenhouse effect. Hence systematic waste management (segregation, composting, recycling, safe disposal) is essential in large cities.

marking_points.point: Open dumping spreads disease and pollutes land, water and air
Landfills release methane, adding to air pollution / greenhouse effect

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Why is composting considered a safe method of waste disposal?
questions.solution: Microorganisms decompose the organic waste; this reduces its size by about 50% and converts it into natural fertilizer called compost or humus.

marking_points.point: Microorganisms decompose organic waste, reducing its size by about 50%
Converted to natural fertilizer (compost/humus)

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Why should we reuse waste?
questions.solution: Recycling needs a lot of energy to dismantle and re-manufacture products; reuse reduces waste, pollution and raw material requirement, saving forests and water.

marking_points.point: Reuse saves energy needed for recycling / reduces waste and pollution and raw material use

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: How can farm waste be made useful?
questions.solution: Used as biofuels (biodiesel, ethanol); sugarcane by-products can substitute plastics (bowls, plates, containers); farm waste can be made into compost/humus for plant growth. (Any one.)

marking_points.point: Any one valid use (biofuel, plastic substitute, compost)

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: How is dumping of waste harmful?
questions.solution: Dumping damages the environment; adjacent areas suffer land, water, soil and air pollution, and surface and ground water get contaminated.

marking_points.point: Causes land, water, soil and air pollution / contaminates water

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question: Mention three ways to reduce waste generation at home.
questions.solution: Avoid single-use plastics; use reusable bottles and cups when travelling; use reusable bags for shopping; donate unused materials to the needy; compost bio-waste in the garden. (Any three.)

marking_points.point: First valid way
Second valid way
Third valid way
